entry.evidence: So far, no attempt has been made to summarise and generalise OC pathways and conceptual ideas into an overarching general concept

steps.action: Surveyed published concepts of marine OC pathways, such as the microbial pump, the microbial loop and BCP sub-concepts, and noted that they focus on selected pathways and partly overlap.
steps.quote: lead to concepts that complement each other (focusing on different processes or pools), but also promote partly overlapping sub-concepts

steps.action: Stated the gap: no overarching general concept summarises the structures of the marine OC cycle.
steps.quote: So far, no attempt has been made to summarise and generalise OC pathways and conceptual ideas into an overarching general concept

steps.action: Noted that existing comprehensive schematics are visually incongruent; some detach processes from their products, such as DIC.
steps.quote: Existing concepts, especially those aiming at a more comprehensive representation of the marine OC cycle, are often not visually congruent

steps.action: Chose a qualitative approach: summarise and generalise known pathways, then compare and condense them into linguistic and visual structures.
steps.quote: we propose stepping back from quantitative, specific, and numerically advanced research and summarising and generalising what is known about the marine OC cycle

steps.action: Posed three guiding questions: which pathways exist, which structures can be condensed, and which processes, pools and agents are embedded in them.
steps.quote: (1) What are the different pathways for an OC compound in marine systems? (2) Which structures can [...] ?

steps.action: Fixed the scope of the concept: no carbonate system, an initial position in surface water, timescales and fluxes ignored, all pathways treated as equally possible, and OC pools (POC, DOC, VOCs, rDOC, DIC) defined from the literature.
steps.quote: We consider all pathways as being equally possible by assuming that each carbon compound finds the conditions for each pathway at the same time.

steps.action: Built a literature-based pathway concept (Supplement S1) by collecting and mapping OC pathways from a non-systematic literature review.
steps.quote: collecting and mapping the different pathways that an OC compound can “take” within the marine OC cycle based on a non-systematic literature review

steps.action: Explained the condensation procedure (functional segments shared by groups of pathways define structures) with a town–lagoon–beach analogy.
steps.quote: we use as an analogy a town with a sandbank separated by a lagoon

steps.action: Compared the mapped pathways. Distinguished closed loops from open loops and identified six functional segments (A–F), keeping the rDOC segments although this is not the strict minimum.
steps.quote: We identify six functional segments that are necessary to describe the desired structures

steps.action: Added spatial information, because segment A cannot say where a position change ends: five spaces were defined (SLS, WCS, USS, LSS, AS).
steps.quote: to unambiguously define structures that account for the differences described above we need to add spatial information

steps.action: Defined three closed remineralisation loops (SLRL, WCRL, USRL) and two rDOC loops (SrDOCL, LrDOCL) by unique combinations of segment sequences and spaces (Table 2, Fig. 1).
steps.quote: we now define three closed remineralisation and two rDOC loops

steps.action: Added two separation rules (the space of ultimate remineralisation sets the loop; rDOC leaving the SLS belongs to the LrDOCL) so that each pathway is counted once.
steps.quote: To avoid double counting when assigning pathways like this to one of our defined loops, two separation rules apply.

steps.action: Defined four open loops (AICL, AOCL, LSICL, LSOCL) for carbon leaving the marine system.
steps.quote: We define four structures of open loops.

steps.action: Synthesised from the literature the processes, pools and agents embedded in each functional segment (Fig. 2, Table 3).
steps.quote: we now add and describe global processes, pools, and agents embedded in each functional segment

steps.action: Showed that higher-resolution structures follow from the embedded pools, for example six pool-based SLRL structures.
steps.quote: for SLRL, six structures can be defined based on the carbon pools involved

steps.action: Translated the Giering and Humphreys (2020) BCP definition into the concept: classified it in the WCRL/AICL, then resolved pools and process subsets (Fig. 3a–d) and compared these with earlier BCP concepts.
steps.quote: we classify the BCP as part of the WCRL or the corresponding AICL

steps.action: Identified ambiguities in the BCP definition (the depth of the 'ocean interior', the inclusion of DOC) and suggested subdividing the WCS to refine it.
steps.quote: illustrates where the BCP concept shows ambiguity and may need to be refined to concretise which pathways belong to the BCP

steps.action: Contrasted the concept with earlier visual OC schematics, whose decoupling of DIC transport can imply that more export always means more sequestration.
steps.quote: this visual decoupling can lead to the false impression that increased transport of OC to the deep ocean always leads to increased sequestration

steps.action: Kept the concept as a general skeleton of OC structures, stating its limits: no quantification or forecasting, loss of complexity, ambiguous symbols.
steps.quote: our concept identifies general structures of all pathways

tree.answer: Many marine OC pathways, described by fragmented and overlapping concepts
No; pathways assembled from the literature
Define overarching structures (loops) of all OC pathways
No stated rivals; existing partial concepts treated as complements
None; the concept makes no predictions
Set by definitional assumptions (scope, spaces, equal possibility of pathways)
Not tested; one illustrative application to a BCP definition
Concept proposed and kept as a framework
Review file not supplied; acknowledgements thank two referees

end.claim: Marine OC pathways can be condensed into three closed remineralisation loops, two rDOC loops and four open loops, defined by sequences of six functional segments across five spaces; the scheme serves as a tool to compare and integrate concepts such as the BCP.

decisive_move.sentence: Comparing and condensing the literature-based pathways into six functional segments and, with the spaces, into the closed and open loops creates the structures that are the paper's claim.

gates.evidence: The pathways come from a non-systematic literature review (§3.1 ¶1) and no hypothesis directed their collection. The BCP translation (§4 ¶2–¶7) is presented as an application example, not as a test the concept could fail. Nothing was fixed in advance; the resolution of the structures is called 'a matter of choice' (§3.1 ¶7).

imports.item: The need to identify basic unifying structures in a science (Scheiner and Willig 2011)
Graphics and conceptual models as tools for disseminating information and promoting discussion (Margoluis et al. 2009)
Conceptual models to reduce miscommunication in education and across disciplines (Fortuin et al. 2011; Heemskerk et al. 2003)

novelty_claims.quote: So far, no attempt has been made to summarise and generalise OC pathways and conceptual ideas into an overarching general concept
our concept decomposes the complexity of OC pathways by defining new universal structures
But we provide a new tool to systematise these considerations and make them more comparable.

limits: Supplements S1 (the literature-based pathway concept) and S2 (the schematic of methodological steps) were not supplied. The non-systematic review does not report search terms, sources, or how many pathways were mapped, so the completeness of the pathway set cannot be judged. No review file or discussion was supplied, so only the final-paper sequence is coded. No check of the result is performed: no alternative condensation, no inter-coder comparison, no test against independent pathway sets. The BCP translation is an illustration and is not coded as a V check, so V is none. claim_status 'capability_characterized' is the nearest category for a conceptual tool; its performance is shown by one worked example, not measured. Composition 'none_fits': this is a conceptual synthesis with no rivals, no crucial test, and no repeated traces or capability. Sub-claims: the ambiguity of the Giering and Humphreys (2020) BCP definition (§4 ¶5) is an interpretive point with no status beyond best reading (inference). The higher-resolution structures (§3.2 ¶18, Fig. 3) are illustrative, status none. The authors themselves state that the concept cannot quantify or forecast (§4 ¶11).

disagreements.target: BCP definition by Giering and Humphreys (2020)
disagreements.support: Translating the definition into the loop syntax shows that its spatial constraint ('ocean interior') and its inclusion of the DOC pool are ambiguous, so pathways may be wrongly included or excluded.
disagreements.quote: illustrates where the BCP concept shows ambiguity and may need to be refined to concretise which pathways belong to the BCP

disagreements.target: Existing comprehensive OC schematics (Steinberg and Landry 2017; Cavan et al. 2019; Anderson and Ducklow 2001; Boscolo-Galazzo et al. 2018)
disagreements.support: The authors point out that these figures represent processes at inconsistent levels of detail and omit or detach products, while granting that the figures serve their own research focus.
disagreements.quote: visually detach processes from their products, such as DIC, or do not mention some products in the figures at all

disagreements.target: Earlier visual OC concepts that transport DIC to depth without resolving its fate (as discussed by Boscolo-Galazzo et al. 2018)
disagreements.support: Citing Gnanadesikan and Marinov (2008), the authors argue that export does not necessarily increase storage, so decoupled schematics can mislead.
disagreements.quote: this visual decoupling can lead to the false impression that increased transport of OC to the deep ocean always leads to increased sequestration

disagreements.target: Traditional, physically focused BCP concepts (e.g. Hansell and Carlson 2001; De La Rocha 2006)
disagreements.support: The authors note that these concepts neglect higher trophic levels and do not explicitly include DIC uptake and remineralisation, and cite recent work on the role of biota in the carbon cycle.
disagreements.quote: The role of organisms, particularly higher trophic levels, was considered quantitatively secondary and was therefore neglected.

alternatives_considered.chosen: Qualitative concept treating all pathways as equally possible
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Resolving the amount of carbon passing through pathways or their probabilities
alternatives_considered.reason: The concept is meant to be qualitative and structural

alternatives_considered.chosen: Six functional segments, including the rDOC segments B and C
alternatives_considered.reason: rDOC is relevant to the climate system and to very different phenomena and processes

alternatives_considered.chosen: Five spaces (SLS, WCS, USS, LSS, AS)
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Subdividing the WCS, or omitting the spatial extent entirely
alternatives_considered.reason: The choice of spaces depends on the intended resolution of the structures

alternatives_considered.chosen: No separate rDOC loop in the upper sediment; sediment rDOC included in the LrDOCL
alternatives_considered.reason: Temporal scales of rDOC produced in the sediment and in the water column overlap

alternatives_considered.chosen: Upward diffusion of non-refractory DOC from the sediment not included in the functional segments
alternatives_considered.reason: Upward movements are not common to all pathways of the remineralisation loops

alternatives_considered.chosen: Ocean interior of the BCP interpreted as the WCS, excluding the USS
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Depth-constrained definitions (export below 100 m, sequestration below 1000 m); including the upper sediment
alternatives_considered.reason: The definition gives no further depth constraint

alternatives_considered.chosen: DOC resolved in the BCP illustration
alternatives_considered.reason: DOC is a relevant carbon flux to the deep sea and the definition does not exclude it
